steps.u: Memory of the search service climbs until it is OOM-killed after about two days. Find the leak.

steps.a: Tens of thousands of retained closures and listeners: something adds an event listener per request without removing it.

steps.r: function proxy(req,res){ const upstream = pool.get(); upstream.on('error', onError); upstream.pipe(res); } // upstream returned to the pool, listener never removed

steps.a: The upstream socket is returned to a pool and reused, but each request adds a new error listener that is never removed. That is the leak. I have found the cause but this session ends with the diagnosis; the fix touches the shared pool code owned by another team.

reference.summary: Traced a two-day memory growth to an event listener added to a pooled upstream connection on every request and never removed, using heap snapshot diffs; the cause was found but not fixed because the pool code belongs to another team.
facts: heap snapshot diff showed many retained closures and listeners
listener added per request on a pooled connection
fix not made in this session
specific: event listener leak on pooled connections

decisions.choice: stop at the diagnosis and not change the pool code
decisions.reason: the pool code is shared and owned by another team
